evidence.note: Created an explicit six-item task list decomposing the framework into ordered subsystems: package/bin/exports, main Vite plugin (plugin-rsc/react + environments), app-router scanning, pages-router + SSG/ISR, all next/* shims, then run-and-fix-tests. Dependency-sensible ordering (resolution/plugin foundation before routing before test), but scope-oriented rather than tied to per-milestone done-criteria.
TaskUpdate status transitions (completed/in_progress) show the agent tracked milestone state across the build, sustaining the decomposition through the horizon.

Built package.json, plugin, all shims, both routers, entries, and CLI/build before running any test (first run only at step 389) — a big-bang integration, not a minimal one-route vertical slice proven under dev first. Verification collapsed into a single terminal milestone (step 124).

After the test harness failed, the agent re-planned: packed vinext, installed fixtures, launched dev servers and probed routes manually — modest revisiting of approach under integration reality, though prompted by tooling failure rather than proactive milestone re-sequencing.

reasoning: The agent identified the major subsystems (module/plugin resolution, app router, pages router, shims, CLI/build) and sequenced them in a defensible dependency-aware order via an explicit tracked task list, with a rough terminal notion of 'done' — squarely the level-5 anchor. It did not establish a minimal end-to-end path (one route under dev) before layering features, instead building everything then testing once, and lacked per-milestone done-criteria tied to concrete fixtures, which keeps it below level 8. Some later re-planning under integration failure nudges it slightly above a flat requirement-mirroring list but not to a 6-plus, so it lands at 5.
